name: Heidelberg University
description: Heidelberg University (Ruprecht-Karls-Universität) is a public research university in Heidelberg, founded in 1386 and Germany's oldest university. It is a comprehensive university spanning the humanities, natural sciences, law and medicine.
whyIncluded: Its medical degree is on the Singapore Medical Council's list of registrable basic medical qualifications, and Germany is among the ten destinations with the most Singaporean students abroad (about 640 in the UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS; UNESCO is the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) data for 2022-24).

livingCosts.summary: A national average for students in Germany from the German Academic Exchange Service, as the university publishes none. Covers rent, food, transport and personal costs for 12 months; excludes health insurance and fees.
livingCosts.notes: The university publishes no itemised cost-of-living estimate for Heidelberg, so this is DAAD's 'Average expenses of a German student' (national average, DZHW 22nd Social Survey 2023): rent incl. utilities EUR 410; food EUR 198; transportation EUR 89; personal = recreation/culture/sports 65 + clothing 46 + working materials 31 + telephone/internet/licence 32 + other 144 = EUR 318. Excludes health insurance (100), tuition (76) and semester contribution (36). DAAD is the German Academic Exchange Service, not the university, so marked secondary. Heidelberg's own page only gives a total of 'min. EUR 992 per month' (the residence-permit minimum) with no breakdown.

programmes.name: Computer Science (Informatik) B.Sc.
programmes.summary: Annual tuition of EUR 1,500 per semester charged to non-EU students by the state of Baden-Württemberg, plus the compulsory semester fee. No separate application fee.
programmes.notes: Baden-Württemberg tuition fee for non-EU/EEA students with a foreign university entrance qualification: EUR 1,500 per semester x2 (in force since winter 2017/18; EU/EEA students and holders of a German entrance qualification are exempt). Compulsory fees = semester fee EUR 189.80 per semester x2 (administrative fee 80 + Studierendenwerk 95 + student body 10 + nextbike 2.30 + theatre flatrate 2.50), from https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/en/study/management-of-studies/semester-fees. Language of instruction: German, partly English. 2024/2025 history: the tuition page states the EUR 1,500 fee has applied since 2017/18; the semester fee of those years was not found, so history entries carry tuition only (current compulsory fees are used).

programmes.name: Rechtswissenschaft (Staatsexamen)
programmes.summary: Annual tuition of EUR 1,500 per semester charged to non-EU students by Baden-Württemberg, plus the compulsory semester fee. The degree takes about five years, so multiply by five.
programmes.notes: Baden-Württemberg tuition fee for non-EU/EEA students with a foreign university entrance qualification: EUR 1,500 per semester x2 (in force since winter 2017/18; EU/EEA students and holders of a German entrance qualification are exempt; it applies to state examination programmes too). Compulsory fees = semester fee EUR 189.80 per semester x2 (administrative fee 80 + Studierendenwerk 95 + student body 10 + nextbike 2.30 + theatre flatrate 2.50), from https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/en/study/management-of-studies/semester-fees. 2024/2025 history: the tuition page states the EUR 1,500 fee has applied since 2017/18; the semester fee of those years was not found, so history entries carry tuition only (current compulsory fees are used). Undergraduate-entry state examination degree, standard period 10 semesters (Faculty of Law subject page, which also quotes the EUR 189.80 semester fee); an integrated LL.B. can be awarded on the way. Language of instruction: German. Winter intake only.

programmes.name: Medizin, Studienort Heidelberg (Staatsexamen)
programmes.summary: Annual tuition of EUR 1,500 per semester for non-EU students, plus the semester fee, over about six years and three months. Places are nationally restricted, with a small quota for non-EU applicants.
programmes.notes: Baden-Württemberg tuition fee for non-EU/EEA students with a foreign university entrance qualification: EUR 1,500 per semester x2 (in force since winter 2017/18; EU/EEA students and holders of a German entrance qualification are exempt; it applies to state examination programmes too). Compulsory fees = semester fee EUR 189.80 per semester x2 (administrative fee 80 + Studierendenwerk 95 + student body 10 + nextbike 2.30 + theatre flatrate 2.50), from https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/en/study/management-of-studies/semester-fees. 2024/2025 history: the tuition page states the EUR 1,500 fee has applied since 2017/18; the semester fee of those years was not found, so history entries carry tuition only (current compulsory fees are used). Undergraduate-entry state examination degree at the Medizinische Fakultät Heidelberg: standard period 12.5 semesters, 'at least six years and three months' (subject page, which also quotes the EUR 189.80 semester fee). Admission is nationally restricted; non-EU applicants with a foreign entrance qualification compete in a preliminary quota. Language of instruction: German. Ruprecht-Karls-Universität Heidelberg (Medizinische Fakultät Heidelberg) is on the Singapore Medical Council's list of registrable basic medical qualifications; the separate Mannheim faculty is not the listed body.

programmes.name: Psychologie B.Sc. (100%)
programmes.summary: Annual tuition of EUR 1,500 per semester charged to non-EU students by the state of Baden-Württemberg, plus the semester fee. Taught mainly in German, and places are limited by grade.
programmes.notes: Baden-Württemberg tuition fee for non-EU/EEA students with a foreign university entrance qualification: EUR 1,500 per semester x2 (in force since winter 2017/18; EU/EEA students and holders of a German entrance qualification are exempt). Compulsory fees = semester fee EUR 189.80 per semester x2 (administrative fee 80 + Studierendenwerk 95 + student body 10 + nextbike 2.30 + theatre flatrate 2.50), from https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/en/study/management-of-studies/semester-fees; the programme page also lists 'Fees and contributions 189.80 EUR / Semester'. Same fee page and figures as Heidelberg's existing programmes, whose history rows are copied. 2024/2025 history: the tuition page states the EUR 1,500 fee has applied since 2017/18; the semester fee of those years was not found, so history entries carry tuition only (current compulsory fees are used). Programme: Psychology - Bachelor 100% (polyvalent B.Sc., Faculty of Behavioural and Cultural Studies), https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/en/study/all-subjects/psychology/psychology-bachelor-100: standard period 6 semesters, winter start only, 'primarily German, with some content in English', admission restricted via the dialogue-oriented services procedure (hochschulstart; aptitude test BaPsy-DGPs can count); non-EU/EEA applicants with a foreign entrance qualification compete in a preliminary quota (Vorabquote statute linked from the page). Enables later licensure as psychotherapist with the clinical master's.

programmes.notes: Baden-Württemberg tuition fee for non-EU/EEA students with a foreign university entrance qualification: EUR 1,500 per semester x2 (in force since winter 2017/18; EU/EEA students and holders of a German entrance qualification are exempt). Programme: Psychology in Research and Application - Master's Course, https://www.uni-heidelberg.de/en/study/all-subjects/psychology/psychology-in-research-and-application-masters-course: Master of Science, consecutive, 4 semesters, winter start only, 'Mainly German, partly English', admission restricted (requires a psychology bachelor's of at least 180 ECTS). Chosen as the broad non-clinical master's; Heidelberg also offers M.Sc. Psychology in Clinical Psychology and Psychotherapy (licensure track).
